newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Nature body says Zaire wildlife threatened by war.
newsitem.headline: Nature body says Zaire wildlife threatened by war.

text.p: A major nature protection body said on Monday the survival of unique animals like white rhinos, mountain gorillas and okapi would be threatened if fighting in Zaire spilled over into wildlife reserves.

The Swiss-based World Wide Fund for nature (WWF) said its Director-General Claude Martin had appealed to the Zairean government and rebels holding regions in the east to keep the conflict out of reserves and national parks.
Areas threatened by fighting "represent a unique heritage for the people of Zaire and the world", Martin wrote in the January 24 letter, a copy of which was released in Geneva.
The appeal was sent amid reports that Zairean government forces were beginning a counter-offensive against the rebels of the Democratic Alliance of Forces of Liberation.

"Destruction of parks' wildlife must be avoided. It remains crucial that the integrity of the parks be respected," said Martin in an implicit appeal to both sides to keep their troops out of the reserves.

The WWF said that among the animal species whose survival would be threatened if fighting spread to these areas were the world's last northern white rhinos, mountain gorillas and okapis -- zebra-like creatures discovered in 1900.
Eastern Zaire's Okapi Wildlife Reserve, with the Garamba and Virunga national parks, have been designated World Heritage Sites by the United Nations.
"The loss of the wildlife and the resources to conserve them would be a far-reaching disaster," said Martin.
